pairs.why: B has the warmer, painterly detail and soft lighting of the real cards, while A is a flat, bare plastic render with an empty set.
A matches the real coral's matte, finely pitted surface and its color spread; B is glossy and swollen like a candy statue, which the lessons mark as wrong.
B's soft satin shading and gentle highlights are closer to the real gloves, while A's hard specular shine pushes it toward glossy toy.
A has the real booth's soft, slightly matte red and muted green; B is crisper and more saturated, like a sharp plastic render.
B's smoother rope with soft gradients and its compact coiled build fit the clean, smooth finish of the real items better than A's more textured, sprawling loops.
A keeps the real card's matte red finish and dark gray base; B adds a glow halo, extra gloss and a purple base that the real card doesn't have.
A's thick, beveled stone top and stronger ground shadows sit a little closer to the chunky real table, though both carry similar marble veining.
B's water droplets on the fruit and its glassier plate echo the real card a bit more, but both use a side view where the real card looks down from above.
